methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Terra Drone, founded by Toru Tokushige, is a publicly listed company on the Tokyo exchange operating in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The valuation exercise confronts a constrained comparable universe: while seven private companies operate within Drones & Autonomous—including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro—no public peers exist in this sector. This absence of public trading data materially limits methodological options.

The peer-median approach, typically the primary triangulation method, is not applicable here. The seven identified private-sector peers lack sufficient clustering by stage, proximity, or valuation tier. Applying the all-sector median across Drones & Autonomous would introduce substantial selection bias, as the peer set spans disparate funding stages and business models without the required minimum of three comparable datapoints within any narrow filter. This structural constraint—zero public comps and zero sufficiently granular private comp clusters—prevents reliable multiple-based valuation.

The analysis cannot produce a supported valuation range given available data. Key uncertainties center on Terra Drone's relative positioning within the private peer universe (stage, revenue, burn profile, path to profitability) and the absence of public market pricing for any Drones & Autonomous operator. Any valuation synthesis would require either (1) additional disclosure of Terra Drone's financial metrics and stage relative to named peers, or (2) expansion of the comp universe to adjacent autonomous systems sectors with established public trading.
